names.official: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis

summary: Saint Kitts and Nevis waives visas for citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, most Commonwealth countries and much of Latin America — normally for up to 90 days — while CARICOM nationals enter freely for six months. Every foreign visitor, visa-exempt or not, must obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA, USD 17) online before travel. Nationals of the 67 countries and territories on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa-required list need a visa, applied for online through the Ministry of National Security's e-visa platform.

fee.notes: Single-entry fee per traveller, plus payment and other fees; faster processing costs more. Mandatory for every foreign visitor, children included. A traveller who arrives without one can apply on arrival but pays the expedited fee.

currencyLimits.text: Cash worth about USD 10,000 or more (or the EC dollar equivalent) must be declared to Customs on arrival and departure. Confirm the current threshold before traveling with large sums.

notes: Firearms and ammunition require a permit arranged in advance; stray rounds found in luggage are treated as a criminal matter.
Camouflage-patterned clothing is restricted across much of the eastern Caribbean and can be confiscated on arrival.
Fresh produce, plants and meat products are controlled. Declare anything agricultural.
Drug offenses carry heavy penalties and apply to visitors in the same way as residents.

payments.text: Hotels, restaurants and supermarkets in Basseterre, Frigate Bay and Charlestown take cards. Minibuses, beach bars, the Nevis ferry and market stalls want cash. US dollars are accepted widely but change comes back in EC dollars.

safety.text: Saint Kitts and Nevis is calm for visitors and the tourist areas see little serious crime, though the Federation has periodic spikes in gang-related shootings between locals in parts of Basseterre. Petty theft from beaches and unlocked cars is the usual risk.

bestTimeToVisit.text: December to April is the dry season with the most settled weather. Carnival peaks around Christmas and New Year on St Kitts, while Culturama on Nevis falls at the start of August, in the middle of the wetter, stormier months.

tips.text: Hurricane season runs June to November and peaks in August and September. The Federation sits in the main Atlantic storm track. Take insurance that covers storm cancellation and be ready for ferry and flight disruption.

Driving is on the left and visitors must buy a local temporary driving permit, arranged through the traffic department or your rental company against a valid home license. Driving without one voids your rental insurance.

St Kitts and Nevis are separate islands linked by a passenger ferry from Basseterre to Charlestown and a car ferry from Major's Bay. Schedules are limited and change with the weather, so do not plan tight same-day connections to a flight.
The East Caribbean dollar is pegged to the US dollar at about EC$2.70 to US$1. US notes are accepted almost everywhere, but you will normally get change in EC dollars at that rate.

Saint Kitts and Nevis runs the oldest citizenship-by-investment program in the world. If you hold a Kittitian passport obtained that way, expect closer scrutiny when applying for visas elsewhere. The EU has been reviewing visa-free access for Caribbean CBI passports.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Saint Kitts and Nevis?
faq.answer: Most visitors do not. Citizens of the EU, UK, US, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, most Commonwealth countries and much of Latin America are admitted visa-free for up to 90 days, and CARICOM nationals for six months. Nationals of the 67 countries and territories on the Ministry of Foreign Affairs' visa-required list need a visa, applied for online through the Ministry of National Security's e-visa platform. Every foreign visitor, visa-exempt or not, must also obtain an Electronic Travel Authorisation (eTA, USD 17) at knatravelform.kn before travel.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Saint Kitts and Nevis without a visa?
faq.answer: Usually up to 90 days, with the officer writing the actual period on your entry stamp. It can be shorter if your return ticket is sooner. Extensions are handled by the Immigration Department in Basseterre and must be requested before the stamp expires.

faq.question: Is there an arrival form for Saint Kitts and Nevis?
faq.answer: Yes — an immigration and customs declaration covering your address in the Federation, length of stay and any dutiable goods. An electronic version has been offered at times, so check with your airline; otherwise the paper card is handed out on the aircraft.

faq.question: Can Chinese citizens travel to Saint Kitts and Nevis visa-free?
faq.answer: No. The Federation maintains diplomatic relations with Taiwan rather than Beijing, so holders of mainland Chinese passports need a visa arranged in advance, while Taiwanese (ROC) passport holders are admitted visa-free. Confirm the current position with a Kittitian mission before booking.

faq.question: Do I need a yellow fever certificate for Saint Kitts and Nevis?
faq.answer: No. The eTA platform run by the Ministry of National Security says there are currently no vaccination requirements to enter. WHO's list still shows a certificate requirement for arrivals from yellow fever risk countries, so if you are coming from one, carrying your certificate costs nothing.

faq.question: Does CARICOM free movement apply here?
faq.answer: Yes. As a CARICOM and OECS member, Saint Kitts and Nevis grants nationals of member states a definite entry of up to six months on arrival, without a visa and without the onward-ticket checks other visitors face.
